meta.defaultDescription: Market structure training taught by Javier Andrade, a licensed Florida contractor who has been trading for fifteen years. Educational content only, with no promises of results.

hero.title: Market structure, taught by someone who learned it the hard way.
hero.body: Fifteen years trading. One single method: market structure. Nobody here tells you where, when or how to put your money — you learn to read the chart, and the decision is yours.

trust.heading: In short
trust.note: One method: market structure. The same chart everyone else is looking at, read a different way. It works the same in stocks, futures, forex and crypto.

about.heading: Who is behind this
about.body: I did not come from finance. I came from construction: I started very young and became a licensed general contractor and plumbing contractor in Florida. I have been trading for fifteen years, tried many methods, and learned most of it the hard way. In the end I kept one approach: market structure.

program.heading: How the mentorship works
program.body: About three months of live sessions, with a maximum of four students per session. You start from zero: you do not need to know anything about markets or to have ever opened a chart.

one.label: Month 1
one.title: From zero
one.body: An introduction to the markets and the vocabulary they use. What a swing is and how to recognise one on a chart. And the question everything else rests on: what market structure actually is.

two.label: Month 2
two.title: Structure from the inside
two.body: Swing structure and internal structure. This is where the chart starts to read itself: you understand how a move is built instead of memorising patterns.

three.label: Month 3
three.title: Reading the whole chart
three.body: Multi-timeframe analysis, supply and demand, ranges and entries. Everything above comes together, moving from understanding the chart to knowing where and why to act.

program.capacity: I never teach a session with more than four students. It is the number that lets me get to everyone within the same hour, which is why a place is not always available.

tools.title: Economic calendar
tools.intro: The days and times the data that moves the market gets published. Free, no sign-up.
tools.why: Whatever method you use, there are moments in the day when price moves because of a release rather than because of anything you were reading on the chart. Knowing when that happens saves a good few frights.
tools.loadBody: The calendar is provided by TradingView and loads from their servers. That is why it does not load on its own: press the button and it opens right here.
tools.loadNotice: Loading it connects your browser to TradingView, which may set its own cookies.
tools.howBody: Each row is a figure released at a specific time. The importance marker shows the ones that usually move price most. Next to each you will see what was expected and what came out: the gap between those two numbers is what the market reacts to, not the number itself.
tools.disclaimer: This calendar is for information. It does not tell you what to do, or when to enter or leave the market, and it does not suggest that trading around a news release is a good idea.
tools.earningsBody: The other calendar people watch is the earnings calendar: the day a company publishes its quarterly results. Every company does this four times a year, so across the market as a whole it is not an occasional event but four seasons — nearly all the large US companies report within the same few weeks.

jan.label: Mid-January to mid-February
jan.window: Fourth-quarter results from the previous year. The longest season and the one that moves the most, because many companies also give guidance for the year ahead.

tools.earningsWhy: Outside those windows a few companies report most weeks, but only a few. What matters to you is simple: if you are holding a stock, check whether it reports before you plan to close the position. An earnings announcement moves the price all at once, often outside normal trading hours, and no amount of reading the chart sees it coming.
tools.earningsLinkButton: Open the earnings calendar on TradingView
tools.earningsLinkNote: This opens TradingView in a new tab. I cannot embed it here the way the economic calendar is embedded: TradingView does not offer an earnings version for other websites. Sending you to the real thing beats copying dates by hand and letting them go stale.

about.title: About me
about.intro: My name is Javier Andrade, I live in Florida, and I have been trading the markets for fifteen years. I did not come from finance.
about.photoPending: [[PHOTO — needs a real photo of Javier. No stock images.]]
about.story: I started working in construction very young. Over the years I earned two Florida licences: general contractor and plumbing contractor. That means estimates that add up or do not, deadlines you meet or you do not, and jobs where the person who gets it wrong pays for it themselves. That is where I learned to work with a method, long before I knew what a chart was.
about.marketsHeading: How I got to the markets
about.markets: I came to the markets fifteen years ago and, like almost everyone, I started by trying everything: indicators, systems, strategies that worked for a month and stopped working the next. I learned most of it the hard way, by losing. I do not tell you that as an anecdote. I tell you because it is the part almost nobody teaches, and it is exactly what you are going to go through.
about.methodHeading: Why I only teach one thing
about.method: Over time I was left with a single approach: market structure. Not because it is magic, but because it was the only thing that kept working when the market changed, or the asset changed, or the year changed. It is the same chart everyone else is looking at, read differently, and it works the same in stocks, futures, forex or crypto. That is what I teach, and nothing else. I would rather you leave knowing how to do one thing properly than having skimmed twenty.
about.teaching: I teach the classes myself, live, with a maximum of four students per session, because with more than that you cannot get to everyone inside the same hour. We start from zero: I assume nothing. And I say from day one what I think needs saying — this is hard, it takes time, and anyone promising you otherwise is selling you something.
about.not: I do not give signals. I do not manage anyone's money. I am not going to tell you where, when or how to put your money, and I am not going to show you accounts or results to convince you. What I do is teach you to read the chart so that you decide. If what you want is somebody to decide for you, I am not the right person.
about.licence: My contractor licences are in construction, not finance. They do not qualify me as an investment adviser and are not meant to. I mention them because they are public and checkable on the State of Florida register, and because they say something about how I work. Nothing more.
about.cta: If you want to know whether this fits you, write to me and we will look at it with no obligation.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: The questions people ask me before they start, answered the way I answer them.

whatIsTrading.q: What is trading, and how is it different from investing?
whatIsTrading.a: Investing means buying something and holding it for years, expecting it to grow. Trading works with price movements over much shorter horizons: days, hours or minutes. Neither is better than the other, they are different crafts. Trading asks for more time, more study and more tolerance for risk.

experience.q: Do I need experience or a finance background?
experience.a: No. The mentorship starts from zero and assumes nothing. My current students arrived having never opened a chart in their lives. What you do need is consistency: almost nobody quits because they cannot understand it, they quit because they cannot keep the rhythm.

howLong.q: How long does it take to learn?
howLong.a: The fundamentals take about three months of steady work. Reading a chart comfortably takes considerably longer than that: years, not weeks. I would rather tell you before you pay. Anyone promising you results in thirty days is selling you a fantasy.

format.q: Are the classes live or recorded?
format.a: Live, on Zoom, twice a week, one hour per session. It is not a recorded course: I am in front of the chart with you, at the same moment, and you can stop me whenever something is not clear. Every session is recorded and sent to you, but the recording is for review — it is not the product.

schedule.q: What days and times are the sessions?
schedule.a: We set the schedule with each group. I am in Florida, Eastern time, and since we are never more than four people it is realistic to find an hour that works for everyone, whether you are in the US, Mexico, Colombia, Chile or Spain.

language.q: Are the sessions in English or Spanish?
language.a: I run separate groups: one in Spanish and one in English. Nobody has to sit through a class in a language they only half-follow.

participate.q: Do I have to speak or turn my camera on?
participate.a: The sessions are participative: you can ask, comment and interrupt me whenever you want, and that is what I expect. If some days you would rather just listen and type in the chat, that is fine too.

missed.q: What if I miss a session?
missed.a: You get the recording of every session, so you can catch up. And if something in that class does not land, you ask in writing or we pick it up at the start of the next one.

between.q: Can I ask questions between sessions?
between.a: Yes. Students get access to a private Discord where they can write to me any time. A question does not have to wait until next Tuesday.

markets.q: Which market do you teach: stocks, futures, forex or crypto?
markets.a: All of them. Market structure does not change with the asset: the same chart reads the same way in stocks, futures, forex or crypto. We look at several markets in the sessions, and over time each student settles on the one that suits them.

timeframes.q: Is this for day trading or for longer holding periods?
timeframes.a: First you learn to read structure. We work on timeframes at the end of the third month, once you have something to decide with. Starting there would be picking a schedule before knowing what you plan to do with it.

platform.q: What do I need in order to follow the classes?
platform.a: A computer, a stable connection and TradingView, whose free version covers everything we do. You do not need six monitors or paid software.

broker.q: Do I need a broker before I start?
broker.a: No. Choosing the platform and getting it set up is part of the mentorship, we do it together. If you already have one, all the better.

studyTime.q: How much time do I need outside the sessions?
studyTime.a: I do not set a minimum, but I give homework, and the people who do it move much faster. Looking at charts on your own between one session and the next is where the learning actually happens.

after.q: What happens when the three months end?
after.a: You decide. You can carry on another month if you feel you need it, or close there, and you can stay in the Discord if you want to keep in touch. There is no lock-in and nothing renews on its own.

places.q: Is there a place available right now?
places.a: It depends on the moment. I never teach a session with more than four students, so sometimes you have to wait for the next intake. Write to me and I will tell you how it stands; if there is no room, I will say so plainly.

signals.q: Do you give signals or copy trading?
signals.a: No, and I do not intend to. Following someone else's signals might hand you the odd win, but it gives you no judgement: it leaves you depending on another person indefinitely. The goal here is that you read the chart without me.

guarantee.q: Can you guarantee I will make money?
guarantee.a: No. Nobody honest can. What I teach is how to read the chart; what you do with that reading afterwards is yours, and so is the risk.

scam.q: How do I know this is not a scam?
scam.a: It is a fair question and you should ask it of anyone selling financial education. What I can offer you: the price is published, the syllabus is published, you know who is teaching, and we talk on a video call before you pay anything. As a general rule, be wary of anyone showing luxury cars, guaranteeing profits, or rushing you with a countdown on the screen.

faq.still: If your question is not here, write to me and I will answer it myself. There is no sales team behind this.
